title: The items a co-author is asked to check
description: What a project offers for human verification: one entry per thing to confirm, with the sentences it appears in and the evidence to confirm it against. A project writes this file (checks/items.json); `manuscript-guard checker build` turns it into one self-contained page a co-author can be sent, and `checker import` takes their answers back. Finding the items is the project's work, because only the project knows where its numbers came from; carrying them to a co-author and recording what came back is the toolkit's.

title.description: What the page calls itself, e.g. the manuscript's short title. The paper's own title is used when this is absent.

groups.description: The kinds of item, in the order a checker should meet them. A group is a question asked the same way of every item in it.

ask.description: The question put to the person checking, in words they need no instructions to answer: "Does the source say this number?"

seconds.description: How long one item of this group takes, for the page's estimate of the work left.

id.description: Stable within a project: an answer refers to it.

title.description: One line, as a list shows it.

facts.description: Label and value pairs shown above the evidence: the value as printed, its unit, where it came from.

sentences.description: Where the manuscript uses it, so a checker sees the claim and not only the number.

mark.description: Substrings to highlight in the sentence.

evidence.description: What to check it against, in the order to try. Everything here is carried into the page: an image by its file, a table or a text excerpt by its content. Nothing is fetched when the page is opened.

caption.description: What this evidence is: the document, the page, the sheet.

note.description: What to look at, or a warning that the value could not be highlighted.

file.description: image only: a path, relative to the items file, of a PNG, JPEG or SVG. Carried into the page, so it need not travel separately.

grid.description: table only: rows of cells as strings, the first rows being the table's headings.

row_labels.description: table only: a label for each row, printed down the left, e.g. a spreadsheet's row numbers.

target.description: table only: the cell to outline, as [row, column] counting from zero.

lines.description: text only: the lines around the value, each [number, text].

text.description: quote only: a passage of the source, as published. What a reader of the manuscript's sentence has to compare it against.

line.description: text only: the line to mark.

rows.description: facts only: label and value pairs.

already.description: Why this item needs no checking, where someone has already done it: the sentence is shown instead of asking again.
